description: ROUTE a symptom to the provider behaviour that explains it. Use this when the user names a provider or a domain (payments, email, auth, SMS, subscriptions) and you need to know what that provider ACTUALLY does — not what its docs say, and not what can be inferred from reading the integration code. Reading the code tells you what your app does with a field. It cannot tell you what the field MEANS at the provider — whether a line item is a seat count, whether a 200 body carries ok:false, whether an event can arrive out of order. That is the class of bug this routes. Returns {spec, workflow, scenario, confidence, reasoning} plus `next_actions`: a typed list of what to call next, with arguments pre-filled. Follow it rather than improvising the next step.

hints.description: Optional caller-supplied overrides. Each field short-circuits the corresponding detection step.

scenario.description: Force a specific failure scenario name.

intent.description: The developer's free-form prompt as they typed it. Don't pre-process or shorten — the router benefits from the full phrasing (capture timing, geo cues, failure mode language).

name: guide
